subject.title: fix(doctor): persist safe migrations before runtime timeouts

question: Should Doctor durably write a validated migration candidate before runtime-backed diagnostics, accepting that later diagnostics can still fail after the migration is persisted?
rationale: This is an intentional upgrade and recovery contract change, not a mechanical correctness question: it determines when `doctor --fix` may alter user configuration despite a later nonzero result.

options.title: Accept the early-write recovery contract
options.body: Merge after confirming that a valid pre-diagnostic migration should persist even when a later runtime health diagnostic exits nonzero.

options.title: Preserve all-or-nothing Doctor writes
options.body: Keep the existing final-write-only contract and pursue a narrower change that makes the runtime timeout non-fatal instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the early-write recovery contract
recommendation.body: Merge after confirming that a valid pre-diagnostic migration should persist even when a later runtime health diagnostic exits nonzero.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned current change author has the most direct context on the intended write and recovery semantics.
